chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan, from Ali ibn Asbat, from 'Ala' ibn Razin al-Qalla', from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I asked him about a man upon whom death was approaching, so he freed his slave boy and made a bequest, and it was more than one-third. He said: The manumission of the slave boy is upheld, and the deficiency is taken from what remains.
ai.seo_question: What happens to a bequest exceeding one-third when a slave is freed on deathbed?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Istibsar, Imam al-Sadiq clarifies the priority of manumission over bequests when a dying person frees a slave and leaves a will exceeding one-third of the estate. The ruling establishes that the slave's freedom is immediately executed and valid, with the excess bequest amount deducted from the residual estate, reflecting the Shia juristic principle that manumission holds precedence over general legacies. This distinction highlights the spiritual merit of freeing a slave in the final moments of life, a key topic in Usul al-Fiqh discussions on inheritance and wills.
